findings.claim: The fallback in GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T> now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing TypeAccessException. Under MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, a dictionary or set keyed by an arbitrary user type is deserialized with a non-collision-resistant comparer, so attacker-chosen keys can cause hash-flooding. This removes a security guard and is unrelated to REQ-2129.

receipt_plan.detail: Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterEdgeCaseReceipts.UntrustedData_RejectsNonHashResistantKeyType: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.GetEqualityComparer<CustomKey>() must throw TypeAccessException. It passes on base and fails on head.

findings.claim: Contractless member collection ignores any MessagePack or DataContract attributes on T. When T carries [MessagePackObject] with [Key]/[IgnoreMember] (or [DataContract]/[DataMember]), the generated formatter still serializes every public read-write member under its name as a string key. An [IgnoreMember] property is therefore serialized and the [Key(0)] int keys are discarded. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured'.

receipt_plan.detail: Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterEdgeCaseReceipts.GeneratedFormatter_HonoursIgnoreMemberOnFormattedType: compile ProjectA.MyType ([MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] Value, [IgnoreMember] SecretToken) into a metadata image, then run MessagePackGenerator on a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class for it. The generated formatter must not mention SecretToken; on head it does.

findings.claim: The generator does not deduplicate between generated formatters and TypeCollector output. If T is declared in the same compilation and is itself a [MessagePackObject], TypeCollector emits its own formatter for T and GeneratedFormatterCollector adds a second ObjectSerializationInfo for the same data type. The resolver then registers two formatters for one type, which causes a duplicate-key/switch conflict or makes formatter choice depend on order.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:60-76 adds the GeneratedFormatterCollector model next to the Collect(typeSymbol) models without excluding data types already collected. Verify with a test that declares [MessagePackObject] class T and [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> in one compilation plus a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver], then compiles and resolves T.

findings.claim: IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. A [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class nested in a non-partial outer class, or declared private inside one, passes validation. The generated 'partial class' part is then emitted inside regenerated containing types (CS0260 on the non-partial outer type), or the resolver cannot instantiate the inaccessible formatter. The user gets a compile error instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.IsPartial (lines 291-297) inspects only formatter.DeclaringSyntaxReferences, and Formatter = new QualifiedNamedTypeName(formatter) carries the containing types into EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces. Test: class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} } plus a resolver, and expect MsgPack019 rather than CS0260/CS0122.
